first.summary: The diff removes the only `payment_method_types` usage, the `checkout.sessions.create` call at src/trpc/controller/index.ts:102. The other named call sites (the `subscriptions.retrieve` calls and `billingPortal.sessions.create`) don't use this parameter and correctly need no change. The problem is that a plain deletion changes behaviour. The session now falls back to dynamic payment methods, so customers see whatever is enabled in the Stripe Dashboard instead of exactly card and PayPal. That may drop PayPal, which must be enabled and eligible for recurring payments, or add methods that weren't offered before. Passing `allowed_payment_method_types: ['card', 'paypal']` would keep today's behaviour. The checks prove nothing: typecheck (6 errors) and build (1 failure) fail the same way before and after, and no checkout session is created against Stripe. The needs-review grade fits.

The methods offered in subscription checkout now depend on Dashboard settings, so PayPal may disappear or other methods may appear. Use `allowed_payment_method_types: ['card', 'paypal']` to keep the current set, or confirm the Dashboard config matches.

The removal only takes effect on API version 2026-09-30 (endive). If the Stripe client pins an older `apiVersion` or SDK version, the parameter is still accepted and this change isn't yet forced. The change and any version bump should land together, and the replacement field should exist in the installed SDK's types.
Typecheck and build fail identically before and after (6 and 1 failures), so they say nothing about whether this call compiles or works. No test or live call exercises `checkout.sessions.create`.

concerns.issue: Line ~105 renames payment_method_types to allowed_payment_method_types. The quoted changelog does not mention this, and I don't know it as a Checkout Session create param. If it doesn't exist, the API rejects the call (unknown parameter) and checkout breaks for every user. This changes behaviour beyond what the upgrade forces. Confirm it against the v23 types and API reference, or revert it.

Line 50 calls subscriptions.retrieve and was named as affected, yet it is unchanged. If it reads subscription.current_period_end (typical for a getUserSubscriptionPlan helper), it will be undefined under the new API version, giving a NaN date or a wrong isSubscribed/isCanceled result.

The Stripe client probably pins an old apiVersion literal, such as '2023-10-16'. That would fail typecheck against v23. If it stays pinned at runtime, responses keep the old shape, so subscription items would lack current_period_end and the new webhook code would produce invalid dates. Check what the client is constructed with and align it with 2026-09-30.endive.

Lines 47 and 66 use subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end with no optional chaining, while the line just above uses items.data[0]?. An empty items array would throw inside the webhook and Stripe would retry. A multi-item subscription silently takes the first item's period.

Line 13 calls constructEvent, and the changelog mentions a change to the verifyHeader default tolerance. Nothing tests signature verification or a live webhook delivery. Event payloads also follow the webhook endpoint's API version, not the SDK's, so any fields read directly from event.data.object need checking.
stripe@23 requires Node >=20 and has @types/node >=20 as a peer dependency. Confirm the deploy runtime (Vercel or another host) and the repo's @types/node version meet this.
qs was removed and several transitive deps were flipped to dev: true because stripe no longer depends on them. This is probably fine, but confirm nothing in production code imports qs directly.

concerns.issue: Line ~105 renames `payment_method_types` to `allowed_payment_method_types` in `stripe.checkout.sessions.create`. Neither the stated API change nor the changelog quote calls for this. As far as I know, `payment_method_types` is still a valid Checkout Session create param, and I don't know of an `allowed_payment_method_types` param. If the name is invented, the call fails with an 'unknown parameter' error from Stripe, or TS rejects it. Either way the subscription checkout flow breaks. It needs a source, or a revert.

Lines 47 and 66 now read `subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end` with no optional chaining. The line just above uses `items.data[0]?.price.id`. If there are no items this throws a TypeError at runtime, the webhook returns 500, and Stripe retries. Under strict TS settings it may also be a type error. Moving from top-level to item-level is semantically correct only for single-item subscriptions.

The `invoice.payment_succeeded` branch casts `event.data.object` to `Checkout.Session` and reads `.subscription`/`.metadata`. In newer API versions `Invoice.subscription` moved to `parent.subscription_details.subscription`. This is pre-existing and probably already short-circuits on the missing `metadata.userId`, but the version bump makes it worse and the PR doesn't touch it. Renewals may never update `stripeCurrentPeriodEnd`.

`new Stripe(...)` sets no `apiVersion`, so every request now uses the SDK's pinned 2026-09-30.endive version instead of the v14-era version. That silently changes request and response shapes for every call: `subscriptions.retrieve`, `billingPortal`, `checkout`. Separately, webhook payloads follow the endpoint's configured version, which may not match the new types.

`constructEvent` is called with the default tolerance, which the changelog says changed. Incomplete bodies now throw `StripeConnectionError`, but the handler doesn't distinguish it from other errors. None of this is exercised by the checks.

stripe 23 requires Node >=20 (see the lockfile engines field). Confirm the deploy runtime (Vercel or other) is on Node 20+. The lockfile also drops `qs` and re-flags `call-bind`, `get-intrinsic`, `side-channel` and others as dev-only. That is fine only if no other prod dependency needs them.

concerns.issue: textToImage (~line 348) now returns `data:image/png;base64,...` strings for gpt-image models. Before, it returned short expiring OpenAI URLs. Each string can be multiple MB, and it goes back through the /images API route to imageGenerationService and then into whatever the DALL·E tool stores (message/plugin state, DB, file upload by fetching the URL). Nothing shows those consumers accept or should persist data URLs. The PNG mime type is also hard-coded, which is wrong if `output_format` is ever set to jpeg or webp. This change also applies to every OpenAI-compatible provider built from this factory, not just OpenAI.

Behaviour changes beyond the rename. Any non-'hd' quality (i.e. 'standard') becomes 'medium', and 'hd' becomes 'high'; cost and latency of gpt-image-2 at these tiers differ from DALL·E's. `style` is silently dropped. Portrait/landscape sizes change aspect ratio (1792x1024→1536x1024). `payload` is no longer annotated as OpenAIImagePayload, so the 'high'/'medium' values bypass the type checker. Whatever server route consumes this body and passes it to `client.images.generate` was not checked.

Only the `model` union changed. `quality`, `size` and `style` still use the DallEImageQuality, DallEImageSize and DallEImageStyle types, and the doc comments still describe DALL·E. The payload actually sent ('high'/'medium', 1536 sizes, no style) no longer matches this interface, so the types only look right.

The DALL·E 2 and DALL·E 3 cards were removed and replaced by a gpt-image-2 card with no `pricing`, so any cost display or usage accounting for image generation loses its data. The listed resolutions ('1024x1024','1024x1536','1536x1024') are not confirmed against the deprecation source. Users or saved settings that reference 'dall-e-3' have no migration or fallback.
CHAT_MODELS_BLOCK_LIST still filters 'dall-e' but not 'gpt-image'. As a result, gpt-image-2 returned by `models.list()` will show up as a chat model in the fetched model list.
